function: Joint learning of active-RIS phase shifts and amplitudes, BS receive beamforming, and offloading/local energy split to maximize sum computation rate (pp. 1, 3).
system: BS with 4 antennas, active RIS with 60 elements, 10 single-antenna IDs, uplink FDMA-NOMA, 1 MHz bandwidth; carrier frequency not stated (p. 2, Table I p. 4).
method: Actor-critic PPO deep reinforcement learning (on-policy), reward equal to the sum computation rate; two-ID pairing precedes it (pp. 3-4, Table I).
data_channel: Custom simulator: log-distance path loss, Rayleigh fading for BS-ID links and Rician for the others, perfect CSI; no dataset or measurements (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Single simulated scenario (5 m user cluster, RIS at origin, BS at 50 m); sweeps of RIS elements, energy budget, RIS position; no unseen-condition test (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: A2C. Other benchmarks: passive RIS, OMA (FDMA), pure NOMA without pairing; their optimizer is not stated; no non-learned optimizer or random RIS (pp. 4-5).
metrics: Sum computation rate (Mbps) versus RIS elements, energy budget, RIS position; training reward convergence (episodes); energy partition parameter versus bandwidth (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Training O(TLξ²), prediction O(Lξ²), with T steps per episode, L layers, ξ neurons per layer; no runtime or parameter count (p. 4).
q1_support: p. 4: "Small-scale fading follows Rayleigh for BS-ID channels and Rician for others." Own simulator with log-distance path loss; no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO, or measured data is named.
q2_support: p. 5: "SCR is shown as a function of the number of reflecting elements N." Sweeps of N, energy budget, and RIS position are plotted, but the paper never says that an agent trained in one condition is tested in another, or adapted.
q3_support: p. 4: "We compare the sum computation rate (SCR) of the proposed scheme against four benchmarks". p. 5: "(4) A2C, employing the Advantage Actor-Critic algorithm (A2C) [15]" is the only learned baseline; passive RIS, OMA and pure NOMA are scheme variants with no stated non-learned optimizer, and there is no random/fixed-RIS or optimization baseline.
q4_support: p. 4: "is O(TLξ 2 ), where T denotes the number of steps per episode" for training, and "the complexity reduces to O(Lξ 2 )" for prediction.
q5_support: p. 4: "Small-scale fading follows Rayleigh for BS-ID channels and Rician for others." The channels come from the authors' own simulator (Table I, p. 4); the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset or measurements.
notes: Included in area 3: the PPO agent learns the RIS phase shifts/amplitudes and the receive beamforming jointly with the offloading energy split (p. 1: "we jointly optimize the energy allocation for offloading and local computing, RIS phase shifts, and receive beamforming"), so it passes the above_phy check. Table I (p. 4) was read from the page image because the text extraction omits it. q3 is 0 because the passive RIS, OMA and pure NOMA benchmarks are not stated to be non-learned (the benchmarks' solver is not described, possibly PPO as well); A2C is compared on the sum computation rate (p. 5, conclusion: around 10% and 27% higher than A2C and pure NOMA). q2 is 0 because the paper does not state that a trained agent is tested on unseen conditions (inference: a different N changes the state size, so each point of the sweep over N probably needs its own training).
